blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We introduce NeuralSRNF, a novel framework for the statistical shape analysis and generation of genus-zero 3D and 4D objects that undergo nonrigid deformations. Traditional methods rely on complex and computationally expensive nonlinear elastic metrics that measure bending and stretching. Recent advances in elastic shape analysis achieve computational efficiency by mapping input 3D shapes to the space of Square Root Normal Fields (SRNFs) where the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric approximates the partial elastic metric, significantly facilitating the process of computing geodesics and summary statistics. SRNFs, however, are not invertible, and the numerical algorithms used to map SRNFs back to the original space of surfaces remain computationally very expensive and often lead to approximate results. This paper addresses this fundamental SRNF inversion problem using a novel neural representation, termed NeuralSRNF. Unlike the commonly used numerical SRNF, NeuralSRNF is (1) continuous, and thus resolution-agnostic, enabling full functional shape analysis, (2) more accurate, and (3) computationally more efficient as it can compute inverse SRNF maps along a geodesic path in less than 3 3 s compared to over 10 10 min for the numerical SRNF. We demonstrate, using various datasets, the utility and efficiency of the proposed NeuralSRNF in multiple elastic 3D and 4D shape analysis tasks such as geodesic computation, deformation transfer, statistical summaries computation, and 3D shape generation. We show that it outperforms competing methods on most evaluated datasets and metrics by a wide margin in both accuracy and computational efficiency. The source code and additional results are available at https://awaisnizamani16.github.io/awais/NeuralSRNF/ .

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: Shape is an important geometric property of natural and manmade objects. Understanding differences and similarities between the shapes of objects has many applications in computer vision, augmented reality, biology, and anatomy. Shape analysis focuses on quantifying such differences or similarities, and characterizing shape variability within a population of 3D and 4D objects using probability distributions. Traditional techniques achieve this by treating the shape of an object as a point on a Riemannian shape space equipped with a proper elastic metric that measures bending and stretching. This way, the dissimilarity between two shapes can be defined as the optimal amount of bending and stretching that one needs to apply to one shape in order to align it with the other. State-of-the-art methods that follow this general pipeline exhibit two fundamental limitations. First , they treat 3D and 4D shapes as discrete surfaces and thus the metric is not invariant to the quality of the discretization. Second , the metric, which is nonlinear, is computationally very expensive to evaluate; thus, it becomes impractical for the statistical analysis of large shape datasets.

blocks.en:
Recent advances in elastic shape analysis achieve computational efficiency by mapping 3D shapes to the space of Square Root Normal Fields (SRNFs) [ 16 , 17 , 20 ] where the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric approximates the partial elastic metric, significantly facilitating the process of computing
geodesics and summary statistics. SRNFs, however, are not invertible as there is no analytical expression for the inverse SRNF for arbitrary points in 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} , and the injectivity and surjectivity of the SRNF map remain to be determined. Thus, one cannot transfer geodesics and statistical analysis conducted in the SRNF space back to the original space of surfaces. While numerical algorithms have been used for the SRNF inversion [ 20 ] , they remain computationally very expensive and often lead to approximate results.

blocks.en: This paper addresses this fundamental SRNF inversion problem using a novel neural representation, termed Neural Square Root Normal Fields (NeuralSRNF). Focusing on genus-0 surfaces, which cover a wide range of shape classes, ranging from human bodies to animals, our key insight is to treat such surfaces as continuous functions parameterized using an MLP. This way, SRNFs become continuous functions. We then propose a novel network architecture that learns how to recover surfaces from their SRNF maps using a Conditional MLP. Unlike the commonly used numerical SRNF [ 20 ] , NeuralSRNF is continuous. Thus, it is resolution-agnostic, enabling full functional shape analysis. The proposed approach is more accurate and computationally more efficient as it can invert SRNF maps along a geodesic path in less than 3 3 s compared to over 10 10 min for the numerical SRNF [ 20 , 29 ] .

blocks.en: In summary, the main contributions are as follows: • We treat genus-0 surfaces as continuous functions parameterized using MLPs. This provides a resolution-agnostic representation, enabling full functional shape analysis. • We propose a novel network architecture that provides a practical solution to the theoretical SRNF problem by learning to recover a valid surface from its SRNF representation. We achieve this using a conditional MLP defined using DINOv2 encoded features and Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM). Compared to [ 20 ] , ours is more than 100 100 times faster and more accurate. • We develop a set of computational tools for geodesic computation, deformation transfer, statistical summarization of 3D and 4D shape collections, and 3D shape generation.

blocks.en: II Related work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Statistical 3D shape analysis methods treat the shape of a 3D object as a point in a high-dimensional shape space equipped with a metric that measures physical deformations; see [ 21 ] for a detailed review of the state-of-the-art. Early approaches that are based on active shape models [ 9 ] and morphable models [ 3 , 11 ] assume that the shape space is Euclidean and use the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric to compute geodesics and perform statistical analysis using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). These methods, however, are only suitable for rigid objects or objects that undergo small elastic deformations since the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric does not quantify elastic deformations.
Later, more expressive metrics have been introduced to capture and quantify large nonrigid deformations. For example, Kilian et al. [ 18 ] use a metric that penalizes deviations from rigidity and isometry. Drawing from the elasticity theory in physics, Wirth et al. [ 42 ] and Zhang et al. [ 45 ] modeled stretching using the Cauchy-Green strain tensor and bending via differences in shape operators. Windheuser et al. [ 41 ] measured bending through variations in the mean curvature, while Heeren et al. [ 15 ] used differences in the second fundamental form for bending and changes in the first fundamental form for stretching.
blocks.zh:
统计三维形状分析方法将三维物体的形状作为高维形状空间中的点,并配有测量物理变形的度量标准;关于最新技术的详细回顾,见[21]. 基于主动形状模型[9]和可变模型[3,11]的早期方法假设形状空间为欧几利得,并使用L 2\mathb{L}^{2}度量衡计算大地测量学并使用主要成分分析(PCA)进行统计分析. 然而,这些方法只适合刚性物体或发生小弹性变形的物体,因为L 2\mathb{L}^{2} 度量衡不能量化弹性变形.
后来,采用了更多的表达度量法来捕捉和量化大型非刚性变形. 例如,Kilian et al. [18] 使用一种惩罚偏离刚性和同位素的衡量标准。 引自物理学中的弹性理论,Wirth et al. [42]和张等. [45] 使用Cauchy-Green菌株拉伸的模型,通过形状操作器的差异弯曲. Windheuser等 (英语). [41] 通过平均曲率的变化测量弯曲,而Heeren等人则测量了弯曲。 [15]使用第二种基本形态的差异来弯曲,第一种基本形态的变化来拉伸.

blocks.en:
While being highly expressive, these physically motivated metrics are computationally intensive since geodesic computation and statistical summarization all require solving nonlinear optimization problems. Jermyn et al. [ 16 , 17 ] introduced a more efficient approach by showing that the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric in the space of SRNFs is equivalent to a partial elastic metric defined as a weighted sum of bending and stretching. This significantly reduces the computational complexity: instead of working in the original space, one can map all the input shapes to the SRNF space, perform the analysis tasks on that space using the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric, and finally map the results back to the original space of shapes. The main theoretical limitation, however, is that this inverse mapping has no analytical expression, and its injectivity and surjectivity are yet to be established. Laga et al. [ 20 ] addressed this by using a numerical approach. The method, however, is computationally expensive, and results in approximate solutions.
This paper addresses this inversion problem using a learning approach, leading to a significantly faster and more accurate solution than the state-of-the-art.
blocks.zh:
这些物理动力指标虽然具有高度的表达性,但在计算上是密集的,因为大地测量计算和统计汇总都要求解决非线性优化问题。 Jermyn等人[16,17]引入了更有效的方法,显示SRNFs空间中的L 2\mathbb{L}^{2}度量衡等于部分弹性度量衡,定义为弯曲和拉伸的加权总和. 这大大降低了计算的复杂性:人们不是在原始空间工作,而是可以将所有输入形状映射到SRNF空间,使用L 2\mathb{L}^{2}度量衡执行该空间的分析任务,最后将结果映射回原始的形状空间. 然而,主要的理论限制是,这种反向绘图没有分析表达,其注入性和悬浮性尚待确定. Laga等人著. [20] 采用数字方法解决这一问题。 然而,这种方法在计算上费用高昂,导致近似的解决办法。
本文用学习方法解决了这个反演问题,导致比最先进的解决方案要快和准确得多.

blocks.en: Note that statistical shape analysis methods require spatially-registered surfaces. Some methods address this jointly with the statistical analysis [ 16 , 17 , 20 ] . Others assume that the registration is pre-established, e.g., by using functional maps [ 31 , 32 , 13 , 2 , 27 , 7 , 23 , 6 ] .
blocks.zh: 注意统计形状分析方法需要空间注册的表面. 一些方法与统计分析[16、17、20]一起解决这一问题。 其他人则认为登记是预先确定的,例如使用功能地图[31、32、13、2、27、7、23、6]。

blocks.en:
Neural representations [ 33 , 28 , 39 ] leverage neural networks to represent the geometry and appearance of 3D shapes in a resolution-agnostic manner. While they were primarily intended for 3D and 4D reconstruction, and novel view synthesis, some recent papers have begun to explore their potential in statistical shape analysis. In particular, Williamson et al. [ 40 ] showed how
to compute differential properties of neural surfaces and perform
geometry processing tasks on spherical neural representations without upfront discretization. Sang et al. [ 37 , 38 ] used neural implicit functions to learn how to deform a source 3D surface to a target one. Their method, however, requires training for every pair of 3D objects and is therefore computationally very expensive. Nizamani et al. [ 29 ] introduced dynamic neural surface representations for the statistical analysis of 4D shapes. Some recent approaches embed surfaces into a learned latent space and compute geodesics within latent space using ARAP regularizations [ 12 , 10 , 44 ] , Laplace-Beltrami operators [ 22 ] , and path straightening [ 14 ] . These geometric constraints are also computationally expensive.

[ 29 ] but focuses on addressing the SRNF inversion problem using a novel neural representation termed NeuralSRNF. This leads to more accurate results while being significantly faster (up to 100 100 times) compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

blocks.en: III Method
blocks.zh: 三、结 论 方法

blocks.en:
We treat the shape of a closed genus-0 surface f : Ω = 𝕊 2 → 3 f:\Omega=\mathbb{S}^{2}\to\real^{3} , after normalization for translation and scaling, as an element of a pre-shape space ℱ \mathcal{F} . To measure the dissimilarity between two surfaces f 1 f_{1} and f 2 f_{2} in ℱ \mathcal{F} , and subsequently compute geodesic paths, we equip ℱ \mathcal{F} with a Riemannian elastic metric that quantifies the amount of bending and stretching one needs to apply to f 1 f_{1} in order to align it onto f 2 f_{2} . This approach, however, is computationally expensive, making it hard to use in downstream tasks such as the computation of geodesics and statistical summaries. This computational cost stems from two fundamental limitations. First , the computational complexity of the metric scales exponentially with the resolution of the discretization of the domain Ω \Omega . Second , the metric is highly nonlinear. Thus, computing geodesics and summary statistics requires solving complex nonlinear optimizations.
To address the computational complexity issue,
Jermyn et al. [ 16 ] map 3D shapes to the space 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} of SRNFs where the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric in 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} is equivalent to the partial elastic metric in ℱ \mathcal{F} . This significantly simplifies downstream tasks since these can be performed in the SRNF space, using the 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric, and then mapped back to the space of surfaces for visualization. The fundamental problem, however, is that SRNFs are not invertible, i.e., the mapping from the SRNF space to the space of surfaces has no analytical form. Laga et al. [ 20 ] approximate this inversion using a numerical approach but it is very slow and often leads to inaccurate results.

When dealing with non-degenerate closed surfaces, Laga et al. [ 20 ] solved this optimization using a numerical approach. To enable the network to invert any SRNF map, we condition it on the shape latent code x . Unlike DeepSDF [ 33 ] , which learns the latent code in an auto-decoding fashion, our latent codes are pre-computed from the SRNF map of each shape using a pretrained DINOv2 [ 30 ] encoder. III-C Deformation transfer
blocks.zh: 三-C 变形转移

blocks.en:
The proposed framework can be used to transfer deformations across surfaces. This problem can be defined as follows: we are given a source deformation f 1 → h 1 f_{1}\to h_{1} , i.e., a surface f 1 f_{1} that deforms into the surface h 1 h_{1} , and we would like to deform a surface f 2 f_{2} so that it assumes the same pose as h 1 h_{1} , obtaining another surface h 2 h_{2} . Traditionally, this is solved using parallel transport, i.e., we first compute the geodesic between f 1 f_{1} and h 1 h_{1} , and parallel transport it to f 2 f_{2} . This involves computing geodesics in ℱ \mathcal{F} and parallel-transporting them, thus it is computationally expensive.
With the proposed NeuralSRNF, this parallel transport problem can be solved in a very efficient manner. We first map the surfaces to the SRNF space 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} , which has an 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} structure. Then, the SRNF of h 2 h_{2} is given by: Q ⁡ ( h 2 ) = Q ⁡ ( f 2 ) + ( Q ⁡ ( h 1 ) − Q ⁡ ( f 1 ) ) . Q(h_{2})=Q(f_{2})+(Q(h_{1})-Q(f_{1})). (6)

blocks.en:
We first evaluate, quantitatively and qualitatively, the accuracy and performance of the SRNF inversion procedure proposed in this paper and compare it against the numerical inversion procedure proposed by Laga et al. [ 20 ] .
For this experiment, we use test surfaces from the COMA, CAPE, DFAUST, Animal with tail, and Animal without tail datasets. For each dataset, we randomly sample 100 100 test surfaces and convert each surface to the SRNF representation. We then apply the inversion frameworks and report the average of the mean squared distance 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} between the ground-truth and the recovered surfaces using our method and the numerical SRNF method [ 20 ] .

我们首先从数量和质量上评价本文提议的SRNF反演程序的准确性和性能,并将其与Laga等人提议的反演程序进行比较。 [20].
对于这一实验,我们使用来自COMA,CAPE,DFAUST,有尾巴的动物和没有尾巴数据集的动物的测试表面. 对于每个数据集,我们随机抽样100100个测试表面,并将每个表面转换为SRNF代表. 然后,我们应用反转框架,并使用我们的方法和数字 SRNF 方法报告地面真相与恢复的表面之间的平均平方距离L 2\mathb{L}^{2}。

blocks.en: Table I reports the mean, median, and standard deviation of the inversion error and inference time for the five datasets. Thus, our proposed framework is 50 50 to 100 100 times faster than the traditional numerical SRNF [ 20 ] while achieving significantly better accuracy.

blocks.en: Table II reports the pairwise geodesic error. For each pair of source and target 3D shapes, we first compute a geodesic path using LIMP [ 10 ] , NeuroMorph [ 12 ] , SAE [ 22 ] , and the proposed NeuralSRNF. We then take each of the 3D shapes along the geodesic, sample 1000 1000 points, and compute the pairwise geodesic distances ( i.e., distances along the shape surface) between these points. We then define the error as the 𝕃 1 \mathbb{L}^{1} distance between the pairwise geodesics of the source surface and the intermediate surfaces along the geodesic path. A lower error indicates a better geodesic path. As shown in the table, our method achieves lower mean, median, and standard deviation errors compared with the state-of-the-art methods. For a fair comparison, we evaluate each method on the datasets supported by the authors’ released code. LIMP [ 10 ] and NeuroMorph [ 12 ] implementations provide training code for FAUST [ 4 ] , while SAE [ 22 ] provides code for DFAUST [ 5 ] . Therefore, we compare each method only on the supported datasets.

IV-D Summary statistics and 3D shape generation
blocks.zh: IV-D 统计摘要和三维形状生成

blocks.en: We evaluate the performance of the proposed framework in computing summary statistics and generating novel 3D shapes. Given a set of 3D shapes, we first normalize them for translation and scale, and convert each to its SRNF representation. We then compute the statistical summaries in the SRNF space following the algorithm presented in Section III-D , and map them back to the original space ℱ \mathcal{F} for visualization, using our proposed method. We also use the computed mean shape and modes of variation to generate random surfaces in the SRNF space, using Eqn. ( 9 ), and invert them to the shape space ℱ \mathcal{F} using our SRNF inversion approach. Figure 11 shows the statistical mean and the first three modes of variation computed on the animal and human dataset. Figure 12 shows some 3D animals generated using the proposed NeuralSRNF. On the other hand, those computed using the numerical SRNF [ 20 ] have unnatural artifacts such as missing and shrunk limbs.

blocks.en: IV-E Application to 4D surfaces
blocks.zh: IV-E 对4D表面的应用

blocks.en:
We now demonstrate the applicability of the proposed NeuralSRNF to 4D surfaces. A 4D (or 3D + + time) surface is a 3D surface that evolves over time, e.g., a moving 3D body shape, a facial surface that performs some expressions, or a surface of an anatomical organ that grows over time (due to the aging process).
Following [ 29 ] , we represent each 3D surface along a 4D sequence using its SRNF. Thus, a 4D surface becomes curves in the SRNF space. The problem of temporal alignment and geodesics and summary statistics computation between 4D surfaces becomes that of temporal alignment and geodesics and summary statistics computation between curves in the SRNF space, which has an 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} structure, and then mapping the results back to the space of surfaces using SRNF inversion.
blocks.zh:
我们现在证明拟议的神经SRNF适用于4D表面. 4D(或3D + +时间)表面是随时间演化的3D表面,如移动的3D体形,面部表面进行一些表达,或解剖器官表面随时间而生长(由于衰老过程).
在[29]之后,我们用它的SRNF来代表每个3D表面沿着一个4D序列. 因此,一个4D表面成为SRNF空间的曲线. 4D表面间的时间对齐和大地测量学和简要统计计算的问题成为SRNF空间曲线间的时间对齐和大地测量学和简要统计计算的问题,后者具有L 2\mathb{L}^{2}结构,然后利用SRNF反演将结果映射回表面空间.

blocks.en: V Conclusion
blocks.zh: 五 结论

blocks.en: We propose NeuralSRNF, a novel continuous surface-based neural representation that provides a practical solution to the ill-posed SRNF inversion problem. Our solution is computationally very efficient while achieving significantly better accuracy than traditional methods. We further demonstrate how core statistical analysis tasks can be performed in the SRNF space, where the complex elastic metric reduces to an 𝕃 2 \mathbb{L}^{2} metric, facilitating downstream analysis tasks such as geodesic computation, deformation transfer, summary statistics, and shape generation. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results for 3D shape analysis across human body, face, and animal datasets. Importantly, it is up to 100 100 times faster than existing methods while achieving improved accuracy. Although efficient, our approach requires registered 3D surfaces, needs to be trained separately for each shape class, and is limited to genus-0 surfaces.
blocks.zh: 我们提出神经神经神经(NeuralSRNF),是一种新型的连续的地表神经表达方式,它提供了一种实用的解决方案,解决备受不便的SRNF反演问题. 我们的解决方法在计算上非常有效,同时取得了比传统方法更好的明显准确性。 我们进一步演示了如何在SRNF空间执行核心统计分析任务,其中复杂的弹性度量衡缩小为L 2\mathbb{L}^{2}度量衡,为大地测量计算,变形转移,汇总统计,形状生成等下游分析任务提供便利. 我们的方法实现了对人体、面部和动物数据集进行3D形状分析的最新结果。 重要的是,它比现有方法快100倍,同时提高准确性。 虽然效率高,但我们的方法需要注册的3D表面,需要为每个形状类单独训练,并且仅限于genus-0表面.
